literal: Broad in kindness, ample in forbearance; joy and anger did not show on his face.
idiomatic: He was broad-minded and forbearing; joy and anger never showed on his face.

literal: In Taihe twenty-first year he was enfeoffed.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in Taihe 21.

literal: At the beginning of Xuanwu's reign he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, then transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, then Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

literal: Yi was talented in government, clear in judgment, dissecting and deciding the multitude of affairs; he had great renown.
idiomatic: Yi had a gift for government and a clear judgment; he cut through the mass of affairs and won great renown.

literal: Minister of Works Gao Zhao, as the emperor's uncle-in-law, was favored and entrusted; once he monopolized authority, he plotted to remove worthy princes and repeatedly slandered Yi, Yu, and others.
idiomatic: Gao Zhao, the emperor's uncle by marriage, held the post of Minister of Works and won favor until he monopolized power; he plotted against worthy princes and repeatedly slandered Yi, Yu, and the rest.

literal: Yu could not bear his rage and therefore rose in rebellion in Jizhou.
idiomatic: Yu could not contain his fury and rose in rebellion in Jizhou.

literal: Because of Yu's rebellion, he also framed and killed Xie.
idiomatic: Using Yu's rebellion as pretext, he also framed and killed Xie.

literal: Yi feared he could not escape.
idiomatic: Yi feared he would not escape.

literal: Zhao also recorded prisoners to establish private favor.
idiomatic: Zhao also reviewed prisoners to curry private favor.

literal: Yi, taking advantage of attendance at a feast, when the wine was deep, then said to Zhao: "The Son of Heaven's brothers—how many are there, that you blaze on without cease?
idiomatic: At a feast, deep in wine, Yi said to Zhao, "How many brothers does the Son of Heaven have, that you burn on without cease?

literal: In old times Wang Mang was bald-headed, yet by his tie through the Weiyang marriage he seized the Han house.
idiomatic: Wang Mang was bald, yet by his kinship through the Weiyang side he seized the Han throne.

literal: Now your crooked form is plain to see; I fear you will again complete the steps of chaos."
idiomatic: Your bent shape is plain to see now; I fear you will again make the ladder of chaos."

literal: He also said to Emperor Xuanwu: "I have heard that only vessels and names may not be lent to others.
idiomatic: He also told Emperor Xuanwu, "I have heard that only rank and title must never be lent away.

literal: Therefore when the Ji clan performed the Feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, Confucius held it deep reproach;
idiomatic: When the Ji clan offered the Feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, Confucius took it as deep reproach;

literal: when Zhongsun hung the royal bells, Qiu Ming took it as the utmost warning.
idiomatic: when Zhongsun hung the royal bells, Qiu Ming called it the utmost warning.

literal: Surely Heaven is honored and Earth is low; ruler and subject have separate ways.
idiomatic: Heaven is high and Earth low; ruler and subject walk separate roads.

literal: One should stop the first sprout and guard against what buds; let none overstep.
idiomatic: One should choke the sprout and bar encroachment.

literal: As for reducing meals and recording prisoners—these are a ruler's affairs; now the Minister of Works performs them—how is that the meaning of a subject?
idiomatic: Reducing the royal table and reviewing prisoners belong to the ruler; now the Minister of Works does them—what part of that is a subject's duty?

literal: Moreover, if Your Majesty cultivates government and teaching and releases prisoners from litigation, then timely rain may descend and the jade candle know harmony.
idiomatic: If Your Majesty cultivates government and teaching and clears the courts, timely rain will fall and the jade candle of peace will glow.

literal: Why let a bright ruler lose them above while a treacherous minister steals them below?
idiomatic: Why should a bright ruler lose them above while a treacherous minister steals them below?

literal: The root of long chaos lies here."
idiomatic: The root of lasting chaos is here."

literal: Emperor Xuanwu smiled and did not answer.
idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu smiled and said nothing.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's Xiping era he was transferred to Grand Commandant, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaoming's Xiping era he was made Grand Commandant while remaining Attendant-in-Ordinary.

literal: An edict ordered Yi to decide affairs of the Gate and Canon, and also to oversee classical commentary.
idiomatic: An edict put Yi in charge of Gate-and-Canon affairs and classical commentary.

literal: At the time there was a monk Huilian who claimed that chanting water and having people drink it could cure all illnesses.
idiomatic: A monk named Huilian claimed that enchanted water, drunk by the sick, could cure every illness.

literal: Those who came to him with illness numbered a thousand a day.
idiomatic: A thousand sufferers came to him each day.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered food and clothing provided.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered food and clothing supplied.

literal: His support was especially heavy; he was sent to the south of the western city to treat the people's illnesses.
idiomatic: His support was lavish; he was sent south of the western city to treat the people's illnesses.

literal: Yi memorialized in remonstrance: "I have heard that the law sets severe penalties for deluding the masses, and ritual cuts off perverse sorcery—all to make clear the upright position and bar treacherous evil.
idiomatic: Yi remonstrated: "The law sets heavy penalties for deluding the masses; ritual cuts off perverse sorcery—both to mark the upright seat and bar treachery.

literal: In old times at the end of Han there was Zhang Jiao, who also used this art and bewitched his age.
idiomatic: At the end of Han, Zhang Jiao used this same art and bewitched his age.

literal: Judging what he did, it does not differ from today.
idiomatic: Judged by his acts, it does not differ from today.

literal: He could entice the living and bring on the disaster of the Yellow Turbans.
idiomatic: He could lure the living and bring on the Yellow Turban disaster.

literal: For decades the realm was scorched—Jiao was the cause.
idiomatic: For decades the realm burned—and Jiao was the cause.

literal: In old times the charlatan Xinyuan did not ascend the Bright Hall;
idiomatic: The charlatan Xinyuan never reached the Bright Hall;

literal: Wuli the opportunist in the end met execution before the crowd.
idiomatic: Wuli the opportunist in the end met public execution.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because Yi was Xiaoming's worthy uncle, his virtue foremost in all eyes, entrusted him with court government, affairs comparable to the Duke of Zhou and Huo Guang.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling, seeing Yi as Xiaoming's worthy uncle and a man all eyes followed, entrusted him with government on the model of the Duke of Zhou and Huo Guang.

literal: Yi strove with all his strength to support and correct, taking the realm as his own charge.
idiomatic: Yi strove to support and correct the realm and took the empire as his charge.

literal: Commander of the Guards Yuan Cha, the empress dowager's sister's husband, relied on favor and was arrogant and full.
idiomatic: Commander of the Guards Yuan Cha, the empress dowager's brother-in-law, leaned on favor and swelled with pride.

literal: Yi restrained him by law and repeatedly suppressed and demoted him; Cha came to hate him.
idiomatic: Yi restrained him by law and repeatedly suppressed and demoted him; Cha came to hate him.

literal: A partisan of Cha's, Direct Attendant Song Zhun, eager for Cha's intent, reported that Yi plotted rebellion.
idiomatic: Cha's partisan, Direct Attendant Song Zhun, eager to please him, reported that Yi plotted rebellion.

literal: Yi was confined at the Gate; when his attendants and court nobles were questioned, the nobles spoke clearly and he was cleared, then released.
idiomatic: Yi was confined at the Gate; when attendants and court nobles were questioned, they spoke clearly, he was cleared, and released.

literal: Yi, loyal yet slandered, then gathered former loyal and stalwart men and made Records of Manifest Loyalty in twenty scrolls to show his intent.
idiomatic: Loyal yet slandered, Yi gathered former loyal and stalwart men and compiled Records of Manifest Loyalty in twenty scrolls to declare his intent.

literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Zhengguang, Cha and Liu Teng forced Xiaoming in the Xianyang Hall, shut Empress Dowager Ling in the rear palace, and imprisoned Yi in the Gate Office.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhengguang 1, Cha and Liu Teng seized Xiaoming in the Xianyang Hall, shut Empress Dowager Ling in the rear palace, and imprisoned Yi in the Gate Office.

literal: Yi, his crime confessed, was then killed; he was thirty-four.
idiomatic: Once his guilt was recorded, Yi was killed; he was thirty-four.

literal: Court and countryside, noble and base, knowing and not knowing, held grief and lost breath; shock shook far and near.
idiomatic: Court and countryside, noble and base, all who knew him and all who did not, grieved and caught their breath; shock ran far and near.

literal: Barbarians in the capital and those returning, hearing of Yi's death, numbered several hundred who gashed their faces for him.
idiomatic: Barbarians in the capital and those returning, hearing of Yi's death, numbered several hundred who gashed their faces in mourning.

literal: Prince of Guangping Huai, among all princes of Wei from the beginning, was summoned into the separate lodge of the Hualin Garden and forbidden to go out or in.
idiomatic: Prince of Guangping Huai, among all Wei princes from the founding, was summoned to the Hualin separate lodge and forbidden to leave.

literal: He ordered the Four Gates academician Dong Zheng to teach him the classics.
idiomatic: The court ordered Four Gates academician Dong Zheng to teach him the classics.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, he was able to return.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, he was allowed to return.

literal: Prince of Runan Yue loved reading Buddhist sutras and perusing histories;
idiomatic: Prince of Runan Yue loved Buddhist sutras and histories;

literal: his nature was unorthodox, free and hard to fathom.
idiomatic: his nature was unorthodox, untamed and hard to read.

literal: Yue's consort, the Lady Yan, was daughter of the Duke of Donghai.
idiomatic: Yue's consort Lady Yan was daughter of the Duke of Donghai.

literal: She bore one son but received no courteous regard.
idiomatic: She bore a son but won no courteous regard.

literal: There was Cui Yanxia, who by heterodox ways kept company with Yue.
idiomatic: One Cui Yanxia kept company with Yue by heterodox ways.

literal: Together they took immortality drugs of pine and artemisia; at times he went out lightly to gather them and lodged in commoners' dwellings outside the walls.
idiomatic: Together they took immortality drugs of pine and artemisia; at times he went out lightly to gather them and lodged in hovels outside the walls.

literal: He then cut off wine, meat, millet, and rice and ate only wheat porridge.
idiomatic: He then gave up wine, meat, millet, and rice and ate only wheat porridge.

literal: He also ceased the bedchamber and instead favored male beauty.
idiomatic: He also ceased the bedchamber and favored male beauty instead.

literal: He lightly resented his consorts and concubines, even beating them, treating them like maids.
idiomatic: He lightly resented consorts and concubines, even beating them like maids.

literal: When Yue went out, the consort stayed at a separate residence; Empress Dowager Ling ordered an inquiry.
idiomatic: When Yue went out, the consort stayed at a separate residence; Empress Dowager Ling ordered an inquiry.

literal: She was brought in and Yue's conduct was pursued to the end.
idiomatic: She was brought in and Yue's conduct was pursued to the end.

literal: The consort was ill on her bed with the cane; her wounds were not yet healed.
idiomatic: The consort lay ill on her bed with the cane; her wounds were not yet healed.

literal: The empress dowager, because Yue had caned the consort, then ordered a ban.
idiomatic: Because Yue had caned the consort, the empress dowager ordered a ban.

literal: She ordered all imperial princes and the three frontier princes that if a principal consort was ill more than a hundred days, all were to report it.
idiomatic: She ordered all imperial princes and the three frontier princes: if a principal consort was ill more than a hundred days, they must report it.

literal: If any still beat them, their enfeoffment was to be cut on the spot.
idiomatic: If any still beat them, their fief was to be cut on the spot.

literal: When Prince of Qinghe Yi was killed by Yuan Cha, Yue had not the slightest hatred but instead waited on him with mulberry-leaf wine and gave his full private fawning.
idiomatic: When Prince of Qinghe Yi was killed by Yuan Cha, Yue felt no hatred but waited on him with mulberry-leaf wine and fawned with all his private arts.

literal: Cha was greatly pleased and made Yue Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: Cha was greatly pleased and made Yue Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commandant.

literal: On the day of his appointment he went to Yi's son Dan and asked for Yi's robes and curios.
idiomatic: On the day of appointment he went to Yi's son Dan and demanded Yi's robes and curios.

literal: When they did not promptly please him, he summoned Dan and caned him a hundred strokes.
idiomatic: When they did not promptly please him, he summoned Dan and caned him a hundred strokes.

literal: Dan was in mourning hut, his form and breath frail and weak; sudden harsh beating nearly brought him to death.
idiomatic: Dan was still in the mourning hut, frail in body and breath; sudden harsh beating nearly killed him.

literal: He then called "Little son" and personally stroked and comforted him.
idiomatic: He then called "Little son" and personally stroked and comforted him.

literal: Yue then made a great mortar-pestle and set it at the province gate; thieves were at once to have their hands cut off.
idiomatic: Yue then set a great mortar-pestle at the province gate; thieves were to have their hands cut off at once.

literal: People feared his unpredictability and that he could do strange things; thieves and rogues feared him and for a time ceased.
idiomatic: People feared his unpredictability and strange deeds; thieves and rogues feared him and for a time ceased.

literal: When Erzhu Rong raised troops toward Luoyang, Yue then fled to Liang.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong marched on Luoyang, Yue fled to Liang.

literal: Emperor Wu of Liang treated him generously.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang treated him generously.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang died, he was then set up as ruler of Wei, the era name changed to Gengxing.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang died, he was set up as ruler of Wei under the era name Gengxing.

literal: At the beginning of Jiemin, troops were sent to escort Yue and place him on the border to watch for invasion.
idiomatic: At the start of Jiemin's reign, troops escorted Yue to the border to watch for invasion.

literal: When Qi Shenwu had killed the Erzhu clan, because Yue was Xiaowen's son and ought to inherit the great enterprise, he had a man convey his intent.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan had killed the Erzhu clan, holding that Yue, as Xiaowen's son, ought to inherit the throne, he sent a man to convey his intent.

literal: When Yue arrived, he was wild and unrestrained as before, constantly committing faults; they stopped.
idiomatic: When Yue arrived, he was as wild as before and constantly erred; they dropped the plan.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaowu he was appointed Grand Marshal and Defender-in-Chief.
idiomatic: At the start of Xiaowu's reign he was made Grand Marshal and Defender-in-Chief.

literal: Xiaowu, because Guangling had considerable virtue and renown, and because Yue by kin was close in rank and near in territory, inwardly feared and was jealous; therefore he killed him before and after.
idiomatic: Xiaowu, because Guangling had virtue and renown and Yue was close in kin and territory, feared and resented him inwardly and killed him in time.

literal: Posthumously given the Acting Yellow Battle-Ax, Grand Preceptor, Governor of Sizhou, Grand Marshal, and prince as before.
idiomatic: He was posthumously given the Acting Yellow Battle-Ax, Grand Preceptor, Governor of Sizhou, Grand Marshal, and his princedom as before.

literal: Posthumous name: Wén Xuān.
idiomatic: Posthumous title: Literary and Illustrious.

literal: His son Ying, with his father, fled together to Liang and died on the left bank of the Yangtze.
idiomatic: His son Ying fled to Liang with his father and died on the Yangtze's southern bank.

literal: The imperial son Tao, seven years old, died in the first year of Jingming; he was coffined in the Jujian Hall amid the Hualin jujubes and buried east of Empress Wen Zhao's tomb.
idiomatic: The imperial son Tao, seven years old, died in Jingming 1; he was coffined in the Jujian Hall amid the Hualin jujubes and buried east of Empress Wen Zhao's tomb.

literal: Later, to enlarge Wen Zhao's rear mound, he was moved and reburied on the northern ridge.
idiomatic: Later, to enlarge Wen Zhao's rear mound, he was moved and reburied on the northern ridge.

literal: Discussion: Among Wen Cheng's five sons, Anfeng alone bore outstanding repute.
idiomatic: Commentary: Among Wen Cheng's five sons, only Anfeng bore outstanding repute.

literal: Yanming's learning was comprehensive, joined to the beauty of elegant discourse;
idiomatic: Yanming's learning was comprehensive, joined to elegant discourse;

literal: reaching Yong'an, his fortune's track topped the army.
idiomatic: by Yong'an his fortune topped the armies.

literal: In the end he met flight and ruin—also his fate.
idiomatic: In the end he met flight and ruin—also his fate.

literal: Xianwen's sons all gradually received Taihe instruction, yet Xianyang ended in rebellious conduct and Guangling died in the mulberry grove.
idiomatic: Xianwen's sons all received Taihe instruction, yet Xianyang ended in rebellion and Guangling died in the mulberry grove.

literal: A man without propriety—each should hurry to his death.
idiomatic: Men without propriety—each should hurry to his death.

literal: Gaoyang's capacity and art were wanting, yet in the end he bore the pillar and beam; when the timbers broke, in truth the corpse lay in his lack.
idiomatic: Gaoyang lacked capacity and art, yet in the end bore pillar and beam; when the timbers broke, the corpse lay in his lack.

literal: Wuxuan's filiality was his substance; loyalty built his conduct; as for bearing danger in safety and the constancy of seeing off the past and dwelling on what follows, the Duke of Zhou's intent that was not another's, and Huo Guang's faith of a different surname—the facts joined both.
idiomatic: Wuxuan's filiality was his substance and loyalty built his conduct; bearing danger in safety, constancy in seeing off the past and dwelling on what follows—the Duke of Zhou's intent not given to another, Huo Guang's faith though of another surname—he joined both in fact.

literal: Yet in the end merit high shook the ruler; virtue lofty moved custom.
idiomatic: Yet in the end merit so high shook the ruler; virtue so lofty moved custom.

literal: One idle word entered, and in the end he did not keep his life whole.
idiomatic: One idle word entered, and in the end he did not keep his life.

literal: Alas!
idiomatic: Alas!

literal: King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Zhao of Han were not easy to meet.
idiomatic: King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Zhao of Han were not easy to meet.

literal: Beihai's righteousness was dim on the magpie and wagtail; luxury and excess destroyed himself—though disaster rose from the green fly, he also brought the sorrow on himself.
idiomatic: Beihai's righteousness dimmed on the magpie and wagtail; luxury and excess destroyed him—though disaster rose from the green fly, he brought the sorrow on himself.

literal: Hao took as if picking up lost things; ruin did not turn the heel—is it that guarding had no method, or Heaven was about to overturn?
idiomatic: Hao took power as if picking up lost things; ruin came without turning the heel—was guarding without method, or was Heaven about to overturn?

literal: The commoner's violent and fierce nature, from childhood growing to length, in the end was deposed and dismissed and did not obtain his end.
idiomatic: The commoner's violent nature, growing from childhood to manhood, in the end was deposed and did not obtain his end.
